content.comment_body: I have a new [product_name] [article_no] and communication works. Using the update center, the newest version shown was [version_no]. On the [company_name] website, however, there’s a [version_no] available, which works well. Is there some confusion here, or did I overlook something?
It sounds like you may have downloaded the wrong file. Is it possible you selected the "Upgrade" option? That would be [version_no]. If you choose the "Update" option, it should be [version_no].

Hi, I was curious and tried this with my own version. Through the Update Center, which allows installation of additional languages, program expansions, and service packs, I connected to the update address and received this information: 1. English language - [version_no] readme, online help, and user interface; 2. Upgrade [version_no] (add-ons) - upgrade to [version_no] for Windows. In the end, I received the same outcome. [user_name], you were right; although we selected Update, only Upgrade options were shown. Best regards, [user_name]
Hello [user_name], [version_no] is not an official release. For [product_name] [version_no], the following versions were released: [version_no], [version_no], and [version_no].

analysis.insight_summary: Users are experiencing confusion regarding the difference between 'Update' and 'Upgrade' options in the Update Center when updating [product_name] software. Although the latest version is available on the [company_name] website, the Update Center often only displays an older version, resulting in uncertainty and frustration. This discrepancy between web and Update Center offerings undermines user confidence in the update process.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the Update Center to reliably offer the latest official software versions, consistent with the availability on the [company_name] website. They also want clear information about the update process and the versions provided.
